title: Enable row-level security
summary: Row-level security adds a database check for rows accessed through client roles.
introduction: Row-level security adds a database check for rows accessed through client roles. Your task: Explain why the client may see no rows before a read policy exists.
learningObjectives: Explain why the client may see no rows before a read policy exists.
Explain the example for enable row-level security

blocks.text: Row-level security adds a database check for rows accessed through client roles. With it enabled and no suitable policy, ordinary client access is denied.

Use the Supabase local CLI with its required container runtime, then run supabase init and supabase start in a practice project. Use the local URL and public key reported by its status command. SQL runs in the local database tools.

blocks.code: ALTER TABLE public.cma_books ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
blocks.title: Enable row-level security

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: Enabling row-level security activates per-role row checks. A client still needs a suitable policy and table privilege.

blocks.text: The table now uses row-level security. The public client still needs an explicit read policy.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not disable RLS just to make a browser error disappear. Define the intended policy.
